subject: math
title: Likelihood: More Likely, Less Likely or Equally Likely
seo_title: Grade 1 Math Likelihood Worksheets for the BC Curriculum (Free, with Answer Key)
standard_text: Likelihood of familiar life events, using comparative language
meta_desc: Free Grade 1 math worksheets on likelihood for the BC curriculum: use always, sometimes and never for everyday events, find which colour is more likely on a spinner or in a bag, compare two events as more likely, less likely or equally likely, and make predictions. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: More chances means more likely. Fewer chances means less likely. The same chances means equally likely.
key_sub: Always means it happens every time. Sometimes means it may happen. Never means it can’t happen. Count the parts or counters of each colour before you decide.
body_html:
Always, sometimes, never

Some things happen every time. Some things may happen. Some things can’t happen. We use three words.

WordMeaningExample
alwaysIt happens every time.The sun comes up in the morning.
sometimesIt may happen, or not.It rains in Vancouver.
neverIt can’t happen.A dog drives the school bus.
Example

Our hockey team plays today. Will we win?

A team can win or lose. We are not sure.

Answer: We win sometimes.

More likely, less likely, equally likely

Count the parts on a spinner. The colour with more parts is more likely. The colour with fewer parts is less likely. If the colours have the same number of parts, they are equally likely.

Example

Is blue more likely or less likely than red?

Blue has 1 part. Red has 3 parts. 1 is fewer than 3.

Answer: Blue is less likely than red.

A bag of counters works the same way. Look in the bag first. Count each colour.

Example

Which colour is more likely?

3 red and 3 blue. The numbers are the same.

Answer: They are equally likely.

Comparing two events

Think about what usually happens. The thing that happens more often is more likely.

Example

You ride BC Ferries. Which is more likely: a seagull or an orca?

Seagulls are near the ferry on most trips. Orcas come by only sometimes.

Answer: a seagull

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Mixing up more likely and less likelyMore parts or counters means more likely. Fewer means less likely
Saying “never” when there is only a little of a colourIf it is there at all, it can happen
Saying “always” when it only happens a lotAlways means every time, with no other way
Choosing your favourite colourCount the parts or counters of each colour
Thinking 6 is harder to roll than 1Every number on a number cube is equally likely

faq.q: What do Grade 1 students learn about likelihood in BC?
faq.a: In the BC Mathematics Curriculum, Grade 1 students describe the likelihood of familiar life events using comparative language. They say whether something is more likely, less likely or equally likely, and use words like always, sometimes and never.
Equally likely means two things have the same chance. When you toss a coin, heads and tails are equally likely.

faq.q: How can I practise likelihood with my child at home?
faq.a: Put 5 red blocks and 1 blue block in a bag and ask “Which colour is more likely?” Pick without looking a few times to check, then change the blocks and try again.

faq.q: Why does my child mix up more likely and less likely?
faq.a: Many children pick the colour they see least, or their favourite colour. Count the parts or counters together first: the colour with more is more likely, and the colour with fewer is less likely.

sets.title: Everyday events: always, sometimes or never?

items.q: The sun comes up in the morning. Which word fits?
items.e: The sun comes up every morning. Clouds can hide it, but it still comes up. So the word is always.

items.q: A dog drives the school bus. Which word fits?
c: sometimes: dogs can ride a bus
items.e: A dog can’t drive. It can’t happen. So the word is never.

items.q: It is a November day in Vancouver. It rains. Which word fits?
c: always: it rains a lot then
items.e: Vancouver gets lots of rain in November. But some days are dry. So rain on a day is sometimes, not always.

items.q: It snows at the beach on a hot July day. Which word fits?
items.e: A July day at the beach is hot. Snow can’t fall then. So the word is never.

items.q: Tuesday comes after Monday. Which word fits?
items.e: Tuesday comes after Monday every week. So the word is always.

items.q: On her birthday, Zara gets 1 year older. Which word fits?
c: sometimes: only if there is a cake
items.e: Every birthday, you get 1 year older. Cake or no cake. So the word is always.

items.q: Our hockey team plays a game. We win. Which word fits?
items.e: A team can win or lose. Trying hard does not make it sure. So the word is sometimes.

items.q: A popsicle sits in the hot sun. It melts. Which word fits?
items.e: The hot sun melts ice every time. So the word is always.

items.q: The sun shines in the night sky. Which word fits?
items.e: The sun does not shine at night. The bright light is the Moon. So the word is never.

items.q: It is fall at a BC river. You see a salmon jump. Which word fits?
c: always: there are lots of salmon
items.e: You may see a salmon jump, or you may not. So the word is sometimes.

items.q: You visit Stanley Park. Which will never happen?
items.e: A tree can’t walk. That is never. The other things can happen sometimes.

items.q: It is a school day. Which will never happen?
items.e: A fish can’t teach. That is never. Reading, recess and painting can happen.

items.q: You ride BC Ferries. Which will always happen?
c: The ferry flies in the sky.
items.e: A ferry floats on water every trip. That is always. You see an orca only sometimes.

items.q: You ride BC Ferries. Which can happen sometimes?
c: The ferry flies in the sky.
items.e: Orcas swim near the ferry on some trips. So that is sometimes. The other things never happen.

items.q: It is a snow day. Which can happen sometimes?
c: It is a hot beach day.
items.e: You may build a snowman, or you may not. So that is sometimes. The other things never happen.

items.q: It is night. Which will always happen?
items.e: The sky is dark every night. That is always. An owl or a shooting star is only sometimes.

items.q: Owen says, “It always rains in Vancouver.” Is he right?
items.e: Vancouver has lots of rain. But it also has dry, sunny days. So it rains sometimes, not always.

items.q: Nadia says, “It sometimes snows at the beach in July.” Is she right?
items.e: July at the beach is hot. Snow can’t fall there. So it never happens.

items.q: Kai says, “The sun comes up sometimes.” Is he right?
items.e: The sun comes up every morning, even on cloudy days. So it always comes up.

items.q: Leah says, “Our team will always win.” Is she right?
items.e: A team can win or lose. Winning last time does not make it sure. So we win sometimes.

sets.title: Spinners and bags: which colour is more likely?

items.q: Red or blue: which is more likely?
items.e: 3 parts are red. Only 1 part is blue. Red has more parts, so red is more likely.

items.q: Green or yellow: which is less likely?
items.e: Only 1 part is green. 3 parts are yellow. Green has fewer parts, so green is less likely.

items.q: Red or blue: which is more likely?
items.e: 2 parts are red and 2 parts are blue. The parts are the same size. So they are equally likely.

items.q: You pick one without looking. Blue or red: which is more likely?
items.e: There are 5 blue counters and 1 red counter. More blue, so blue is more likely.

items.q: You pick one without looking. Yellow or green: which is less likely?
items.e: There are 2 yellow and 6 green. Yellow has fewer, so yellow is less likely.

items.q: You pick one without looking. Red or blue: which is less likely?
items.e: 3 red and 3 blue. The same number, so they are equally likely. Neither one is less likely.

items.q: Green or purple: which is less likely?
items.e: 5 parts are green. Only 1 part is purple. Purple has fewer parts, so purple is less likely.

items.q: You spin once. Which is right?
c: Red is less likely than blue.
Red is more likely than blue.
Red and blue are equally likely.
items.e: 1 part is red and 3 parts are blue. Red has fewer parts. So red is less likely than blue. Red is there, so you can still get it.

items.q: You pick one without looking. Which is right?
c: Yellow is less likely than purple.
Yellow is more likely than purple.
Yellow and purple are equally likely.
items.e: There are 4 yellow and 2 purple. Yellow has more. So yellow is more likely than purple.

items.q: You spin once. Which is right?
c: Blue and red are equally likely.
Blue is less likely than red.
Blue is more likely than red.
items.e: 2 parts are blue and 2 parts are red. Same number, same size. So they are equally likely.

items.q: You spin once. Which is right?
c: Blue is more likely than red.
items.e: Every part is red. The arrow must land on red. So you will always get red.

items.q: Which colour will you never get?
items.e: The bag has red, blue and yellow. There is no green. So you will never get green.

items.q: Which colour is most likely?
items.e: Count each colour: red 4, blue 2, yellow 1. Red has the most. So red is most likely.

items.q: Which colour is least likely?
items.e: Count each colour: red 1, blue 4, yellow 2. Red has the fewest. So red is least likely.

items.q: On which spinner is red more likely than blue?
items.e: Spinner C has 3 red parts and 1 blue part. More red, so red is more likely. On A, red is less likely. On B, they are equally likely.

items.q: On which spinner are red and blue equally likely?
items.e: Spinner D has 2 red parts and 2 blue parts. The same, so they are equally likely.

items.q: In which bag is blue less likely than red?
items.e: Bag C has 1 blue and 5 red. Fewer blue, so blue is less likely than red. Bag D has more blue, so blue is more likely there.

items.q: In which bag will you always get red?
items.e: Bag D has only red counters. So you will always get red. Bag C has a yellow one too.

items.q: Liam says, “Blue is more likely. It is my favourite.” Is he right?
items.e: 3 parts are red and only 1 is blue. A favourite colour does not change the spinner. Red is more likely.

items.q: Ava says, “I will never get yellow. The part is small.” Is she right?
items.e: There is 1 yellow part. The arrow can land on it. So yellow is less likely, but not never.

sets.title: Compare two events: more, less or equally likely?

items.q: Think about Vancouver. Which is right?
c: Snow in July is more likely.
Rain in November is more likely.
items.e: Vancouver gets lots of rain in November. Snow in July does not happen there. So rain in November is more likely.

items.q: It is July in Kelowna. Which is right?
c: A sunny day is more likely.
items.e: Kelowna is hot and sunny in July. A snowstorm does not happen then. So a sunny day is more likely.

items.q: It is January in Whistler. Which is less likely?
items.e: Whistler is cold and snowy in January. A hot beach day does not happen then. So a hot beach day is less likely.

items.q: You toss a coin. Heads or tails: which is more likely?
items.e: A coin has 2 sides. Each side has the same chance. So they are equally likely.

items.q: You ride BC Ferries. Which is right?
c: Seeing a seagull is more likely.
Seeing an orca is more likely.
items.e: Seagulls fly near the ferry on most trips. Orcas swim by only sometimes. So seeing a seagull is more likely.

items.q: You roll a number cube. 6 or 1: which is more likely?
items.e: 6 and 1 are each on 1 face. So they are equally likely. A big number is not harder to roll.

items.q: It is a clear night. Which will you more likely see?
items.e: On a clear night, you can see stars. The sun does not shine at night. So stars are more likely.

items.q: It is January in Prince George. Which is right?
c: Snow on the ground never happens.
A hot beach day is more likely.
Snow on the ground is more likely.
items.e: Prince George is very cold in January. Snow is on the ground most days. So snow is more likely than a hot beach day.

items.q: Dark clouds fill the sky. Which is more likely?
items.e: Dark clouds often bring rain. So rain is more likely than a sunny day.

items.q: A popsicle sits in the hot sun. Which is more likely?
items.e: The hot sun warms the popsicle. Ice melts when it gets warm. So melting is more likely.

items.q: The teacher picks one name. Mei or Liam: which is more likely?
items.e: Each name is in the hat 1 time. So Mei and Liam are equally likely.

items.q: It is a school day. Which is more likely?
items.e: You read books at school a lot. You never ride an elephant there. So reading a book is more likely.

items.q: Think about Vancouver. Which is right?
c: Snow in July is less likely.
Snow in July is more likely.
items.e: Snow does not fall in Vancouver in July. Rain in November happens a lot. So snow in July is less likely.

items.q: It is a hot July day. Which is less likely?
items.e: There is no snow on a hot July day. So building a snowman is less likely than going to the beach.

items.q: Ryan rolls a number cube. A 3 or a 7: which is more likely?
items.e: 3 is on the cube. 7 is not, so you can never roll 7. So a 3 is more likely.

items.q: It is fall at a BC river. Which will you more likely see?
items.e: In fall, salmon swim up BC rivers. Sharks do not live in rivers. So a salmon is more likely.

items.q: Ryan says, “6 is less likely than 1. It is a big number.” Is he right?
items.e: 6 is on 1 face, just like 1. So they are equally likely. Big numbers are not harder to roll.

items.q: Wei rides BC Ferries. He says, “An orca is more likely than a seagull.” Is he right?
c: No. A seagull is more likely.
Yes. An orca is more likely.
items.e: Seagulls are near the ferry on most trips. Orcas come by only sometimes. So a seagull is more likely. Being big does not make it more likely.

items.q: Chloe says, “Tails is more likely than heads.” Is she right?
items.e: A coin has 2 sides with the same chance. So heads and tails are equally likely.

items.q: It is November in Vancouver. Which is most likely?
items.e: November in Vancouver is cool and very rainy. Hot beach days and snowstorms are rare then. So a rainy day is most likely.

items.q: Kai spins 10 times. What will he probably see?
items.e: 3 parts are red and 1 is blue. Red is more likely. So he will probably see more red than blue.

items.q: Mei tosses a coin 10 times. What will probably happen?
items.e: Heads and tails are equally likely. So she will probably get some of each. A coin has no 3.

items.q: Which colour will you probably pick?
items.e: There are 6 blue and 2 red. Blue is more likely. So you will probably pick blue.

items.q: Mateo puts in 3 more red. Which is more likely now?
items.e: Red: 2 + 3 = 5. Blue: 2. 5 is more than 2. So red is more likely now.

items.q: Hana takes out 2 blue. Which is more likely now?
items.e: Blue: 4 − 2 = 2. Red: 3. 3 is more than 2. So red is more likely now.

items.q: Kai spins 10 times. He gets red 8 times and blue 2 times. Which spinner did he probably use?
items.e: He got a lot more red. Spinner C has 3 red parts and 1 blue part. Red is more likely there.

items.q: Sofia spins 10 times. She gets red 5 times and blue 5 times. Which spinner did she probably use?
items.e: She got red and blue the same. On spinner B, red and blue are equally likely.

items.q: You want green. Which bag is best?
items.e: Each bag has 6 counters. Bag C has 5 green. So green is most likely in bag C.

items.q: Which bag will never give you yellow?
items.e: Bag D has only blue counters. There is no yellow. So you will never get yellow from bag D.

items.q: Which number will you probably get?
items.e: 3 parts have a 1. Only 1 part has a 2. So 1 is more likely.

items.q: Ji-woo rolls a number cube 12 times. Will she roll a 7?
c: Yes, if she rolls a lot.
items.e: The faces show 1 to 6. There is no 7. So she will never roll a 7, even if she rolls a lot.

items.q: It is July in Kelowna. What weather will probably come?
items.e: Summer in Kelowna is hot and sunny. Snow and ice are not likely in July.

items.q: It is January in Prince George. What will you probably wear outside?
items.e: Prince George is very cold in January. Snow is likely. So you will probably wear a warm coat and mitts.

items.q: It is November in Vancouver. What should Noah bring to school?
items.e: Rain is very likely in Vancouver in November. So an umbrella is the best thing to bring.

items.q: Kai goes to Whistler for Spring Break in March. What will he probably do?
items.e: In March there is still lots of snow on the mountains at Whistler. So skiing is most likely.

items.q: It is fall. Olivia visits a BC river. What will she probably see?
items.e: In fall, salmon swim up many BC rivers. Orcas live in the sea, not rivers. So salmon are most likely.

items.q: Dark clouds fill the sky. Should Lucas take his umbrella?
c: No. It is not raining yet.
items.e: Dark clouds often bring rain. So rain is likely. It is not sure, so “always” is the wrong reason.

items.q: Hana loves purple. Which colour will she probably get?
items.e: 3 parts are green and only 1 is purple. Her favourite colour does not change the spinner. Green is more likely.

items.q: Jasleen wants blue. What will probably happen?
items.e: Look in the bag: 5 red and 1 blue. Wanting blue does not help. Red is more likely.

items.q: The school bus comes every school day. Tomorrow is Tuesday. What will probably happen?
items.e: Tuesday is a school day. The bus comes every school day. So the bus will come.

sets.title: Word problems: which is more likely?

items.q: Before a soccer game, the referee tosses a coin. Our captain calls heads. Which is right?
c: Heads and tails are equally likely.
items.e: A coin can land on heads or tails. Each side has the same chance. So they are equally likely.

items.q: Mei gets heads 3 times. She tosses again. Which is right?
c: Heads and tails are still equally likely.
items.e: A coin does not remember. Each toss, heads and tails have the same chance.

items.q: The teacher picks one name from the hat. Which is right?
c: Liam is more likely than Mei.
items.e: Each name is in the hat 1 time. So every name has the same chance.

items.q: Nadia’s name is not in the hat. Which is right?
c: Nadia is more likely than Mei.
items.e: Only names in the hat can be picked. Nadia’s name is not there. So she will never be picked.

items.q: Only Owen’s name is in the hat. The teacher picks one. Which is right?
items.e: There is only one name in the hat. It must be Owen. So Owen will always be picked.

items.q: Emma takes a popsicle without looking. Which is she more likely to get?
items.e: There are 4 red and 2 yellow. More red, so a red one is more likely. There are no green ones.

items.q: Only yellow popsicles are left. Liam takes one. Which is right?
items.e: Every popsicle left is yellow. So he will always get yellow.

items.q: Sofia picks a mitt from the lost and found without looking. Which is right?
c: Red is more likely than blue.
Red and blue are equally likely.
Red is less likely than blue.
items.e: There are 5 blue mitts and 1 red mitt. Fewer red, so red is less likely than blue. Red is there, so she can still get it.

items.q: Owen picks a mitt from the bin without looking. Which is right?
c: Red and blue are equally likely.
Red is more likely than blue.
Red is less likely than blue.
items.e: There are 3 red mitts and 3 blue mitts. The same number, so they are equally likely.

items.q: Our school does the Terry Fox Run in September. Which weather is least likely?
items.e: September can be sunny, cloudy or rainy. A snowstorm is very rare then. So it is least likely.

items.q: At the fall fair, the yellow ball wins a prize. Ava picks one ball. Which is right?
c: Yellow is more likely than red.
Yellow is less likely than red.
Yellow and red are equally likely.
items.e: There is 1 yellow ball and 6 red balls. Fewer yellow, so yellow is less likely than red.

items.q: Arjun wins if he picks red. Which bag should he pick from?
items.e: Bag C has 4 red counters. That is the most red, so red is most likely there. In bag A, he will never get red.

items.q: Simran wins if she lands on blue. Which spinner should she use?
items.e: Spinner A is all blue. She will always get blue. On spinner C, she will never get blue.

items.q: Harjot needs a yellow counter for a game. What can he do?
c: Put a yellow one in the bag.
items.e: There is no yellow in the bag, so he will never get one. Picking again does not help. He must put a yellow counter in.

items.q: Owen goes whale watching near Victoria. Which is right?
c: He may see an orca, or may not.
He will never see an orca.
He will always see an orca.
items.e: Orcas swim in the sea near Victoria. Some trips see them, some do not. So he may see one.

items.q: It is Canada Day. Which will always happen?
items.e: July 2 always comes after July 1. Fireworks and rain happen only sometimes.

items.q: Our team won 3 games in a row. Which is right about the next game?
items.e: Winning before does not make the next game sure. We may win or lose.

items.q: On Sports Day, 6 children run a race. Ethan is one of them. Which is right?
c: Ethan may win, or may not.
items.e: Any of the 6 children could win. We can’t be sure it is Ethan. So he may win, or may not.

items.q: Ryan needs an 8 to win the game. He rolls a number cube. Which is right?
items.e: The faces show 1 to 6. There is no 8. So he will never get an 8.

items.q: Kai leaves his popsicle in the sun on a hot day in Kelowna. Which is right?
c: Melting is more likely than freezing.
Freezing is more likely than melting.
items.e: The hot sun warms the popsicle. Warm ice melts. So melting is more likely.
